documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Auto insurer's claims office called requesting PCP notes related to the 1/2025 accident. Signed patient authorization received by fax this morning, limited to 1/2025-5/2025 visits. Released 1/16/25, 2/11/25 notes and the 4/24/25 work letter. Logged in release of information.

events.reason: high-speed motor vehicle collision with left chest injury

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Large left pleural opacity consistent with fluid, with the trachea and mediastinum shifted to the right. No new rib fracture identified. Healed fractures of several left lateral ribs. Right lung clear. No pneumothorax on this view.
reports.conclusion: Large left hemothorax with rightward mediastinal shift. Old healed left rib fractures.

reports.text: Portable AP chest after left chest tube removal. Left lung expanded. Trace blunting of the left costophrenic angle. No pneumothorax. Mediastinum midline. Old healed left rib fractures.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain
Take 1 tablet by mouth every 8 hours as needed with food

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital Emergency Department. Date of service 06/22/2026.

CC: MVC, high speed.

HPI: 33M arriving by EMS after a high-speed crash. Belted driver, airbags deployed. Left chest pain and short of breath. Known to us from January 2025: left hemothorax and ICU stay with coagulopathy after a prior crash.

PMH: as above; R femur IM nail 2025. Meds: none. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, social alcohol. FH noncontributory, no bleeding disorders.

Arrival vitals: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 28, SpO2 89% RA.

Exam: awake and oriented, anxious, diaphoretic. Left chest: bruising over the lateral wall, diminished breath sounds, dull to percussion. Trachea deviated to the right. Abdomen soft and not distended, no seat belt sign. Pelvis stable to compression. Extremities without deformity; no evidence of long bone fracture.

Labs: Hgb 9.8, Hct 29, plt 250, PT 12 s, aPTT 30 s.
FAST: no free fluid in the abdomen.
CXR: large left hemothorax with rightward shift.

Procedure: emergent left tube thoracostomy, 28 Fr, 5th intercostal space anterior axillary line, with immediate bloody return and improvement in breathing. 2 units PRBC given with improved pressure and heart rate.

Impression: left traumatic hemothorax with hypovolemic shock and tension physiology; chest wall contusion; acute blood loss anemia. Coags normal.
Disposition: admitted to Trauma Surgery.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital Trauma Surgery. Admitted 06/22/2026, discharged 06/26/2026.

Diagnoses: left traumatic hemothorax with hypovolemic shock; left chest wall contusion; acute posthemorrhagic anemia.

Course: Second high-speed MVC in 18 months. Left chest tube in the ED with prompt hemodynamic response after 2 units of red cells; no further transfusion. Coagulation normal throughout. Tube output decreased steadily and the tube came out 06/25; film after showed an expanded lung, no pneumothorax and trace left costophrenic blunting. Pain controlled with oral agents. Ambulating independently.

Discharge labs: Hgb 10.3.

Discharge medications:
- Acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs every 8 h as needed
- Ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 h as needed with food

Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CBC. Trauma clinic 2 weeks with chest x-ray. Incentive spirometer 10x/hour while awake. No lifting over 10 lb for 2 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call. Pt home since Fri after 2nd MVC, L chest tube 6/22-6/25, 2u PRBC. Discharge summary received today. Pain 3/10, using tylenol and ibuprofen alternating. Breathing ok, doing his spirometer. Chest tube site with a small dressing, no drainage, no fever. Meds reviewed, no confusion. PCP visit Wed 7/1 10:00 confirmed.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit, 9 days after a second high-speed crash. Records reviewed: L hemothorax w/ shock and tracheal deviation, ED chest tube, 2u PRBC, normal coags this time, tube out 6/25, d/c 6/26 Hgb 10.3.

S: L chest sore with coughing and rolling over, better each day. Breathing comfortable walking around. No fever, no hemoptysis. Taking acetaminophen 2-3x/day and ibuprofen once a day. Using the spirometer. Leg fine. Out of work this week.

Meds: acetaminophen prn, ibuprofen prn. NKDA.

O: Vitals in flowsheet, SpO2 normal RA. Alert, comfortable. L lateral chest with fading bruise, chest tube site closed and clean. Breath sounds present throughout, minimally decreased at the L base. Heart RRR. Abd soft NT. No calf tenderness.

A/P:
1. L traumatic hemothorax s/p chest tube: doing well. Trauma clinic 7/8 with CXR.
2. Blood loss anemia: CBC and ferritin today. Holding off on iron unless ferritin is low.
3. Chest wall contusion: current analgesics; ibuprofen with food, stop if stomach upset.
Work note through 7/10. RTC prn; CBC again in about 6 weeks.

documents.title: Results from your visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tyler, hemoglobin is 11.4, up from 10.3 at discharge, and your iron level (ferritin 71) is fine this time, so no iron pills needed. Your body will rebuild the rest on its own. Let's recheck the blood count in mid-August; I put in the order, any weekday morning works.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Lungs clear and well expanded. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Old healed left rib fractures. Normal heart size and mediastinal contours.

documents.title: Trauma Clinic Letter
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital Trauma Surgery Clinic. Visit 07/08/2026.

Dear colleague,

Mr. Wilder came back two weeks after discharge for his left hemothorax. He feels well, short of breath only with hard exertion, chest wall soreness easing.

Exam: lungs clear bilaterally. Tube site healed. Mild tenderness over the left lateral chest wall where the bruise was.

CXR today: clear, no effusion.

Hemothorax resolved. Chest wall contusion settling; expect a few more weeks of soreness. May return to work and normal activity, avoid contact sports another 2 weeks. No routine trauma follow-up needed.

Medications: acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Back at work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - went back to work last week, all good. Ribs barely bother me anymore, I haven't needed the ibuprofen in days. HR wants my file updated with a clearance note for full duty, same as last time. Could you send one?

documents.title: Return to work letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

Tyler Wilder (DOB 07/02/1992) has been under my care and was cleared by his surgical team on July 8, 2026. He may work at full duty without restrictions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin is 13.9, back in the normal range. Nothing more to do. See you next month for your physical.
